newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour attacks claimant jobless data as bogus.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour attacks claimant jobless data as bogus.

text.p: The opposition Labour party said Britain's statistics for claimant count unemployment, which on Wednesday showed a seasonally adjusted fall of 35,600 in September, could not be trusted.
Ian McCartney, the party's chief employment spokesman, said a more accurate picture emerged from the Labour Force Survey.

This showed that, while the number of people in employment increased by 210,000 over the last year, 95 percent of those jobs were part-time. Moreover, the number of full-time employees fell by 47,000 over the summer, McCartney said.

In addition, an article in the October edition of the government's Labour Market Trends publication said that of 344,400 people who left the unemployment register in June, only 190,500, or 55.3 percent, went into work, Mccartney said.
The article said approximately 50 percent of those who found work or moved on to sickness benefit re-signed for unemployment benefit within one year, he added.
"The government's claimant count figures are entirely bogus," McCartney said in a statement.
